diagnosis: The structural induction is valid, but `grind` cannot reduce the `substOld` application match when the function and argument are known only through branch equalities. Explicitly splitting that match and its identifier test lets `simp_all` expose the replacement-variable membership case; the remaining constructor cases are discharged as before.
proof_body:
by
  intro v Hin
  induction post <;>
    simp [OldExpressions.substOld,
      Imperative.HasVarsPure.getVars,
      Lambda.LExpr.LExpr.getVars] at *
  case app fn e fn_ih e_ih =>
    split at Hin
    · split at Hin <;>
        simp_all [Imperative.HasVarsPure.getVars,
          Lambda.LExpr.LExpr.getVars]
    · simp [Imperative.HasVarsPure.getVars,
          Lambda.LExpr.LExpr.getVars] at Hin ⊢
      rcases Hin with Hin | Hin
      · rcases fn_ih Hin with Hin | Hin
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inl Hin)
        · exact Or.inr Hin
      · rcases e_ih Hin with Hin | Hin
        · exact Or.inl (Or.inr Hin)
        · exact Or.inr Hin
  all_goals grind
